Haneul Kim

B.S. Computer Science, Machine Learning and AI, California Baptist University

Human-AI interaction, AI and LLM evaluation, grounding, synthetic data generation, and AI applications in biomedicine.

I'm a senior at California Baptist University. Most of my research asks whether language models can be trusted to say what their sources actually support. In the CBU AI and ML Lab, I build citation-grounded QA models for U.S. Army doctrine, where I found a model citing sources in every answer while almost never citing the right ones. That gap between what a metric shows and what a model does is the problem I want to keep working on.

I've also applied machine learning to flood prediction and physiological biometrics, and built production LLM systems in industry.

Research

Five projects across language models and scientific ML

LLM Reliability for Military Doctrine QA

Feb 2026 – Present

ML Researcher, CBU AI and ML Lab (CAiMLL)
Dr. Mark Kim, Dr. Esther Lee, Dr. Shannon Siojo, Dr. Jounsup Park

Training models to answer questions on U.S. Army doctrine with citations that actually support the answer.

  • Grounding
  • LoRA
  • Evaluation
Details
  • Built the data generation, verification, and LoRA training pipeline for a citation-grounded QA model on U.S. Army doctrine.
  • Found the model cited sources in every answer but rarely the right ones (~0.1 F1), and redesigned the dataset to target doctrinal reasoning.
  • Designed answerability-aware augmentation so the model learns when a question can't be answered from its source.

Separate vs. Unified Fine-Tuning for Multi-Document Domains

May 2026 – Present

Undergraduate Researcher, with Kip Park, California Baptist University
Dr. Esther Lee, Dr. Shannon Siojo, Dr. Jounsup Park

Should one model learn many documents, or should each document get its own model?

  • Hallucination
  • Fine-tuning
  • Benchmarks
Details
  • Co-led a study testing whether one unified model or one model per document better reduces hallucination in document QA.
  • Fine-tuned Gemma on three universities' handbooks and built standard and near-miss multiple-choice benchmarks.
  • Found the better strategy depends on difficulty: unified won on standard questions, specialists on harder near-miss ones.

Hydrology and Flood Prediction

Sep 2025 – Present

Undergraduate Researcher, California Baptist University
Dr. Benjamin Sanders

Filling gaps in a mountain rain gauge to feed flood modeling for the City Creek watershed.

  • LSTM
  • PyTorch
  • Time series
Details
  • Built the ML pipeline filling gaps in a mountain rain gauge from a lower-elevation gauge, feeding flood modeling for the City Creek watershed.
  • Built LSTM and CNN-LSTM models in PyTorch; LSTM reached mean R² = 0.758 ± 0.024 over 15 seeds, outperforming CNN-LSTM on R², MAE, and KGE.
  • Replaced a noisy single-split early-stopping scheme with 5-fold chronological cross-validation, stabilizing training across seeds.
  • Benchmarked against 11 regression models and 5 MLPs; a 15-seed LSTM ensemble (R² = 0.766) slightly exceeded the linear baseline (R² = 0.764).
